To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the phage fusion protein-modified liposome targeting efficiency can be optimized by varying preparation protocols, lipid compositions, and phage protein contents.
phage protein modified liposomes with a high affinity for target cells can be prepared by a simple and cost effective method.

the liposomal membrane composition and the preparation protocols are critical factors that influence the targeting efficiency of the phage protein-modifed liposomes and that the optimized liposome formulation can be used as a potential drug carrier in cancer treatment.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a novel and simple approach for the production of liposomes with improved affinity to tumor cells.
the optimization of the phage protein-modification of liposomes for tumor targeting.
the development of a new generation of liposomes with improved tumor targeting efficiency and enhanced drug delivery efficiency.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the optimal formulation of phage liposome for the maximum targeting efficiency is 1:1 (mol/mol) ratio of DPPG to DOPE and 0.5 mol% (mol/mol) of phage protein in the lipid mixture, which can be further tested in vivo.

the phage liposome formulation containing 0.5 mg/ml phage protein, 1.0 mg/ml DPPG, 0.5mg/ml PEG2kPE and 10 mg/ml DSPE-PEG2k-DOPE in the presence of 10% ethanol and 0.2 M sucrose in PBS at 50°C and pH 7.4 for 1h is the optimal formulation.
a combination of phage protein and DPPG with PEG2k in the liposomal membrane is the most promising formulation for phage liposomes to be used in cancer therapy.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the use of a fusion protein consisting of a phage coat protein and a tumor cell-specific peptide as a targeting moiety for the preparation of tumor-specific liposomes is a promising strategy for the development of targeted liposomes.
the phage protein-modifying approach is a promising method for the preparation of tumor-targeted liposomal formulations, which could be used for the development of new anticancer therapeutics.
the targeting activity of phage protein-liposomes can be enhanced by optimizing liposome composition.
The main takeaway from our work is that
phage liposomes with improved tumor targeting activity can be obtained by optimizing the liposome composition.
the phage liposomal system can be optimized for improved target specificity.
phage protein can be used as an alternative to antibodies for the preparation of tumor-targeted liposomal nanocariers.
